plotSections.title: Overview
bullets: Gerk finds Haldor in New Navel and asks him to help Sylan send on bad spirits. Haldor walks with Gerk to Sylan, who is waiting outside the gate, and hears both Gerk’s recap and Sylan’s account.

Haldor treats the party as the stronghold hooligans, confirms Carlkin reported the portal in his house, and writes down a tighter city ban: extradimensional doors, interdimensional doors, and spirit-taking are all prohibited inside New Navel.

plotSections.title: Spirits in Sylan
bullets: Gerk says Sylan sent him to find Haldor because Sylan needs help rounding up bad spirits and sending them to the afterlife. Spirits fly into Sylan, which Gerk compares to a jug; Haldor takes up the phrase spirit jug.

Gerk’s recap: after seeing Carlkin they practiced doors in the woods away from people; Sylan worked a hoard lantern-staff, blinded Gerk, and while Gerk was blinded spirits entered Sylan. Those spirits wanted to go home and said bad spirits were still in town.

Sylan tells Haldor he is a cleric and servant of the Raven Queen, tasked with finding people who escaped their end. He believes he accidentally took six people from New Navel. The party can already see spirits; Ord’s lantern showed him the ones following Sylan, and Sylan sent them on because that was his duty.

Sylan remembers an older humanoid woman, like a grandmother, most clearly and asks if she had already died and if Haldor recognizes her. Haldor says there have been no recent missing persons and asks for features beyond an old humanoid woman. The chunk ends as Sylan tries to recall her.

plotSections.title: Carlkin, the file, and the door ban
bullets: Haldor says Carlkin reported the incident: an extradimensional door, described as a hell portal or pentacle-spewing portal, opened in Carlkin’s commons. Gerk says he fixed the floor and that his other doors had been interdimensional, so he had not expected an extradimensional one.

Carlkin filed charges Haldor calls fandologium charges. Haldor has not worked out the charge. He keeps a file on the whole party labeled stronghold hooligans, says most of it comes from Carlkin, and expects to skip the paperwork if they leave in a day or two.

Haldor reads a notepad notice: extradimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited in the city, practice belongs in the forest, and spirit-jug sucking is not permitted. He hoped Gerk had the interdimensional shackles; Gerk does not. Gerk offers a door to the shackles and Haldor refuses any such door in the city. Sylan is currently outside the gate.

plotSections.title: The beacon bet
bullets: Haldor places the blinding and the spirits in Trigash Forest earlier today, around midmorning. He bet Erwin 25 gold that the giant beacon was a random event; Erwin bet it was the stronghold hooligans. Haldor now owes Erwin the money.

Erwin saw the beacon, then the group flying that way with a new dragon in tow, and about an hour later flying back out. They reached town about forty-five minutes before this talk. The walk from the forest is a couple of miles. Gerk says he walked and is surprised the others flew into town.

plotSections.title: The goose vendor
bullets: Haldor recognizes Joanna’s chicken on Gerk and says she makes good geese. Gerk hates geese, calls them evil little birds, and says he may have threatened the goose vendor, mostly in jest, because the vendor has so many.
Haldor tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. He calls the caged-goose seller a decent vendor who keeps the flock well, and he may refer to that man as Gator.

chronologicalEvents: Haldor, roused from a rest, recognizes Gerk and asks why he is back. Gerk says Sylan tasked him with finding Haldor so bad spirits can be sent home.
Gerk describes spirits flying into Sylan like a jug. Haldor checks that Sylan has not taken anyone from the party and that Gerk is all right.
Haldor notices Joanna’s chicken. Gerk says he dislikes geese and may have threatened the goose vendor, mostly in jest. Haldor warns him not to threaten villagers.

Gerk says Sylan is just outside the gate. On the way, Gerk says they saw Carlkin yesterday. Haldor says Carlkin reported an extradimensional portal in his commons and filed charges, and that the party’s file is labeled stronghold hooligans.

Gerk apologizes, says he fixed the floor, and recounts doorway practice in the woods, the lantern-staff, being blinded, spirits entering Sylan, and those spirits asking to go home while warning of bad spirits in town.

Haldor identifies the place as Trigash Forest and admits he owes Erwin 25 gold over the beacon bet. Erwin saw them fly toward the forest with a dragon and fly back about an hour later; they arrived roughly forty-five minutes ago. Gerk says he walked.
Haldor asks for the interdimensional shackles. Gerk does not have them. Haldor reads a new notice banning extradimensional and interdimensional doors, and spirit-taking, inside the city.

After a short walk, Haldor greets Sylan. Sylan says he serves the Raven Queen, accidentally gathered about six New Navel people, and that Ord’s lantern revealed the spirits following him so he could send them on.
Haldor says there are no recent missing persons. Sylan starts describing an older humanoid woman and tries to remember her features.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: Has not seen Gerk in some time and agrees to go help Sylan sort out the spirit-taking.
Recognizes Joanna’s chicken and knows the caged-goose vendor as a decent seller with a well-kept flock. He tells Gerk not to threaten villagers.

Carlkin reported the portal in his commons, including that Gerk fixed the floor. Carlkin filed charges Haldor has not sorted out. Haldor keeps the party’s file under the label stronghold hooligans and would rather wait for them to leave than investigate.
A notepad notice now prohibits both extradimensional and interdimensional doors in the city and tells Gerk to practice in the forest. Spirit-jug sucking is also forbidden.
He hoped Gerk was carrying the interdimensional shackles and does not want a doorway opened to fetch them.

He bet Erwin 25 gold that the Trigash beacon was a random event and now owes that bet. Erwin told him the group flew out with a dragon and back about an hour later, reaching town about forty-five minutes before this conversation.
He says he knows nothing about gods. No missing persons have been reported recently, and he does not recognize Sylan’s older woman from the description given so far.
personality: Dry and practical. He will hear the spirit problem out, but he avoids paperwork and expects the party to be gone before he has to pursue Carlkin’s complaint.
He is firm about city rules and about not threatening vendors.
quotesThemes: Labels the party file stronghold hooligans.
Extra dimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited within the city limits, and spirit-jug sucking is not permitted either.
openQuestions: Whether he can identify the six people Sylan believes he took, especially the older woman.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Sylan sent him to bring Haldor in so bad spirits can be rounded up and sent to the afterlife.
He still has Joanna’s wicker chicken, hates geese, and says he threatened the goose vendor mostly in jest.
He tells Haldor they saw Carlkin yesterday, that he did not expect the door to be extradimensional, and that he repaired Carlkin’s floor. He offers to apologize and expects Carlkin to yell.
He practiced doors in a safe place away from people, then was blinded while Sylan used the hoard lantern-staff. He did not see the spirits enter Sylan.
He does not have the interdimensional shackles. He walked back from the forest while others flew, and he is surprised they flew into town.
personality: He talks around the spirit problem, compares it to a jug, and defers the real explanation to Sylan. He is apologetic about Carlkin and defensive about the geese.
quotesThemes: Calls geese evil demon little birds and says that is why he bought the chicken.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper, with a cautious bond to the Raven Queen.
notes: He waited outside the New Navel gate while Gerk fetched Haldor.
He tells Haldor he is a cleric of the Raven Queen and one of her servants, tasked with finding people who escaped their end.

He believes he accidentally gathered six people from New Navel while traveling into town or earlier. He does not have their names. He remembers an older humanoid woman, grandmother-like, most vividly because he interacted with her most closely, and he offers to describe the six.
He says the party can already see spirits, but Ord’s lantern let Ord see the ones following Sylan, and Sylan sent them on as his duty. He also says there are bad spirits still to send home.
Gerk’s version adds that Sylan was using the hoard lantern-staff, blinded Gerk, and only then took in the spirits.
personality: He frames the spirit-taking as duty rather than an attack, and he admits he is not sure how the six were gathered.
quotesThemes: I'm a cleric of the Raven Queen, and I am one of her servants, and I've been tasked with finding people that have escaped their end.
openQuestions: Who the six New Navel people are, and whether the older woman had already died.

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: Sylan says Ord was working the lantern in Trigash Forest and that the lantern let Ord see the spirits surrounding Sylan. Sylan calls him a friend and says Haldor would have seen them goofing around by the beacon.

Erwin.existing: New Navel man who won 25 gold betting the Trigash beacon was the stronghold hooligans.
notes: He saw the giant beacon, judged it the stronghold hooligans, and won 25 gold from Haldor.
He saw the group fly toward Trigash Forest with a new dragon in tow, then fly back out about an hour later.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person associated with a lighthouse and shop in New Navel.
notes: He reported Gerk’s portal to Haldor: a hellish or pentacle-spewing extradimensional door in his commons. He also reported that the floor was fixed.
He filed charges Haldor calls fandologium charges. Haldor says Carlkin is grumpy and that most of the collected file on the party comes from him.
Gerk says the visit was yesterday and expects Carlkin to yell if they apologize.
personality: Grumpy, and diligent about reporting the party to Haldor.

Goose vendor.existing: Caged-goose seller two doors down from Joanna.
notes: Gerk says he threatened this vendor, mostly in jest, over how many geese he keeps. Haldor objects and describes him as a decent vendor whose flock is caged and well kept.
Haldor’s line about Gator may be this vendor’s name or a bad hearing of the geese.

Fused lantern-staff.existing: Fused lantern and staff that reveals the Ethereal Plane and draws nearby spirits when the active staff is held.
notes: Gerk calls it a hoard-bought staff, something like a staff of lantern flies. Sylan says Ord activated the lantern.

It let Ord see spirits following Sylan even though the party can already see spirits. Its use in Trigash Forest is tied to the beacon Haldor and Erwin saw, and Gerk was blinded while it was being used.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: Haldor’s latest notice bans extradimensional doors and interdimensional doors inside the city limits. Spirit-taking is also prohibited. Magic practice is directed to the forest outside.
No missing persons have come in recently. Sylan believes six spirits he took were people from here, including an older humanoid woman.
From town, Trigash Forest is a couple of miles and a decent walk. The party’s flyers got back about forty-five minutes before Gerk’s talk with Haldor.
openQuestions: Whether six residents, including an older woman, were among the spirits Sylan took.

Trigash Forest.existing: Forest outskirts where a beacon and spirits that stay back were encountered.
notes: Haldor and Gerk place today’s blinding, lantern practice, and spirit-taking here. The beacon was visible from New Navel. The forest is a couple of miles out, and part of the party flew there and back.

Beacon of celestial darkness.existing: A column of felt darkness that rises while the active staff is held.
notes: Seen from New Navel as a giant beacon in the sky over Trigash Forest. Haldor and Erwin bet 25 gold on whether it was a random event or the stronghold hooligans. Erwin was right, and Haldor owes him.

newTerms.name: Spirit jug
notes: Haldor and Gerk’s name for Sylan taking spirits into himself so they can be sent on. Haldor rules that spirit-jug sucking is forbidden in New Navel.

newTerms.name: Fandologium charges
notes: What Haldor calls the charges Carlkin filed over the portal in his commons. Haldor has not determined what the charge means and is inclined to let it lapse if the party leaves.

newTerms.name: Stronghold hooligans
notes: Haldor’s file name for the party, and the side Erwin took in the 25 gold bet on the Trigash beacon.
